description: Object keys are sorted by UTF-16 code unit; no whitespace.
Sorting applies at every depth; arrays keep their order.
Numbers as JavaScript JSON.stringify writes them: no trailing zeros, exponent form past 1e21, -0 as 0.
Strings as JSON.stringify writes them: only ", \, control characters escaped; non-ASCII kept literal; the hash runs over UTF-16 code units (an emoji is two).
The shipped grocery example rulebook (everything but its fingerprint) hashes to its fingerprint.

findings.message: `checkout_speed` set by Site manager tightens `robot_speed` set by Law and safety: `robot_speed` (set by Law and safety) says limit maxSpeedMps 1; `checkout_speed` (set by Site manager) says limit maxSpeedMps 0.3. Both apply to Inventory robot, Restock robot, Cleaning robot · enter an area, move, dock · Checkout, always. A lower authority may tighten, so this is fine; `robot_speed` never takes effect there. For example: inventory_robot does enter_zone in checkout with peopleInZone=0, localTime="00:00", day="mon".

`shopper_photos_entrance` set by Site manager tries to loosen what `glasses_capture` set by Company sets: `shopper_photos_entrance` (set by Site manager) says allow; `glasses_capture` (set by Company) says deny. Both apply to Shopper · take photos or video · Entrance, always. A lower authority can only tighten, so `shopper_photos_entrance` never takes effect at all. For example: shopper does camera_capture in entrance with peopleInZone=0, localTime="00:00", day="mon".

`staff_audio_back_room` (set by Site manager) says allow; `no_audio_back_room_lunch` (set by Site manager) says deny. Both apply to Staff · record audio · Back room, when localTime in 12:00–13:00. The strictest answer wins, so `staff_audio_back_room` never takes effect there. For example: staff does record_audio in back-room with peopleInZone=0, day="mon", localTime="12:00".
